gate_results.notes: EditMode run at the validated commit b44a34ce481eb9b05464ea7c13d08249234536bd: total 304, passed 292, failed 0, skipped 12. The runner reports Git tree == post-run tree 48068dc834af1de30d9d61cb036cb6f5d1b5db02, so the repository was not mutated by the run, and the XML contains zero test-cases with result=Failed. All six fixtures this gate names ran and none failed: RuinedEntrySceneTests 17 total / 16 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; BoneArchiveSceneTests 5/5/0/0; ChapelOfAshSceneTests 21/21/0/0; LowerVaultSceneTests 22/21/0/1; FinalRoomSceneTests 11/11/0/0; DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests 58/58/0/0. The gate's sprite-binding requirement - which explicitly rejects an assertion that merely counts cells or checks a name - is met by two assertions that bind the committed asset. FLOOR: ChapelOfAshSceneTests.Builder_PaintsFloorTilemapExactlyInsideWallInteriorFaces asserts AssetDatabase.GetAssetPath(floorTile.sprite) equals Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Art/Environment/Source/floors/floor_ChapelOfAsh.png. WALL: ChapelOfAshSceneTests.WallTiles_ResolveToCommittedSourceSpritesWithNoCollider loads the committed Art/Environment/Source/walls/wall_straight.png and wall_broken_stub.png sprites via AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath, asserts both are non-null, then asserts Assert.AreSame object identity against farWallTile.sprite and cutawayWallTile.sprite - reference identity with the committed asset, which is stronger than a path string. The two ignored cases in these fixtures are RuinedEntrySceneTests.CaptureGameplayCameraReview and LowerVaultSceneTests.CaptureGameplayCameraReview, screenshot-capture helpers carrying [Ignore]; neither is an assertion of this gate.

Regression gate: it asserts NSC-045's delivered contract still holds after the tileset swap and does not restate NSC-045's numbers as a fresh claim. The same EditMode run at b44a34ce481eb9b05464ea7c13d08249234536bd carries the committed-scene checks and none failed. 0.5-world-unit sprite-extent-versus-BoxCollider agreement: ChapelOfAshSceneTests.CommittedScene_HasApprovedDoorsAisleLandingStagingAndCoverColliders asserts Mathf.Min(wall.bounds.size.x, wall.bounds.size.z) == 0.5 within 0.001 over the committed wall colliders, and FinalRoomSceneTests asserts wallTile.sprite.bounds.size.y * 0.2 == 0.5 within 0.05, tying the swapped sprite's extent to the same 0.5 world unit. Per-cell transform matrices: FinalRoomSceneTests.CommittedScene_CentralObstacleCarriesTheApprovedTint asserts tilemap.GetTransformMatrix(position) equals Matrix4x4.Scale(1, 0.2, 1) for low-wall cells and Matrix4x4.identity otherwise, per cell. BoneArchiveSceneTests.CommittedScene_ValidatesForComposition asserts the committed BoxCollider bounds equal their expected values. NOT PROVEN by this gate: nothing here re-derives NSC-045's original numbers; it establishes only that the assertions encoding them still pass at this commit.

human_approval.notes: NSC-109 has two completion gates, VAL-001 and VAL-002, and both are automated EditMode gates; the contract contains no human gate, so no human approval is claimed. This follows the shape of NSC-050's record, which states the same thing for two automated PlayMode gates. Recorded by the Game Agent (Integration Steward) on 2026-09-25 at commit b44a34ce481eb9b05464ea7c13d08249234536bd, the tip of the wizard-scale merge where Unity actually ran. The implementation reached main on 2026-09-24 via merge ef2170cdd; base_commit 9a86882e082ad7419cfca4fb39a5abc6c2c317bd is the single merge-base of that merge's two parents, confirmed with git merge-base --all. This record is evidence debt being paid on already-merged work, not a claim that the work landed today. EXPLICITLY NOT CLAIMED, because it would be misleading by omission: Vincent has NOT signed off the appearance of these floor tiles. On 2026-09-25 at 10:12Z he ruled the opposite - that the violet stone palette is WRONG and is to be regraded, floors first - while choosing to ship now and regrade separately. The Art Director owns that regrade. VAL-001 and VAL-002 are binding and geometry gates and are unaffected by palette; they do not assert that the art looks right.
